clue.text: Plan for elephant keeper to be given parking avoiding hospital

indicators.note: avoiding says the hospital letter is kept out, with the parking letter given in its place

parts.note: a mahout is the driver and keeper of an elephant in India
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A zookeeper's plan to get a parking space instead of a hospital bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be given parking avoiding hospital' swaps the H in MAHOUT for P.
explanation.definitionFit: To map out a scheme is to plan it in detail, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Console learner disconnected to help cure failing

indicators.note: failing suggests something going wrong, so the remaining letters are jumbled
disconnected says the learner letter is cut off from the words that follow

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British car, so learner gives L

explanation.surface: A sympathetic note: helping to cure a failing learner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disconnected' takes L out of HELP CURE, leaving HEPCURE, which 'failing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To console someone is to try to lift their spirits, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Intrinsically Latin adorable hound

parts.note: per se is the Latin phrase for intrinsically, by itself
adorable means cute

explanation.surface: A list of words describing a sweet hound dog, perhaps a Latin-named breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin' tells you the word for intrinsically is the Latin PER SE. 'hound' looks like a dog but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hound someone is to harass them relentlessly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Discover mistake — time to oust female!

indicators.note: to oust says the time letter pushes the female letter out and takes its place

parts.note: a defect is a flaw or mistake

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a mistake and declares it's time for a woman to be thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To detect something is to notice or find it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Core of schools covered by bad language syllabus

indicators.note: covered by says the core letter sits inside the word for bad language

parts.note: a curse is a swear word, bad language

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter, here the middle of a seven-letter word

explanation.surface: Swearing has crept into the core school syllabus.
explanation.definitionFit: A course of study is the programme a syllabus sets out, a near-synonym.

clue.text: Shy about once dropping round High Court

indicators.note: about says the shy word goes around what remains

parts.note: chary means wary or shy

indicators.note: dropping says the round letter falls out of the word once

parts.note: a round shape gives O

explanation.surface: A timid figure goes about the High Court, having once dropped round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes the round letter from 'once'; 'about' wraps the shy word around the rest. 'round' looks like a social visit but is the letter shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancery is a division of England's High Court, so the name stands for that court.

clue.text: Wedding is sore point when bride's top goes missing

indicators.note: goes missing says that first letter is taken away

parts.note: a bunion is a sore swelling on the foot

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A wedding becomes a sore point when the bride's headdress disappears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sore point' is literal: a painful bump on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a marriage, so the word serves for a wedding.

clue.text: Football managers' least favourite competition?

parts.note: football managers dread being sacked, so a race to be fired would be their least favourite contest

explanation.surface: A wry question about which contest football bosses would hate.
explanation.walkthrough: A sack race is a children's sports-day race in sacks; managers are said to get 'the sack' when fired.
explanation.definitionFit: The playful definition reads a children's hopping race as a contest to be dismissed first.

clue.text: One beset by longing over losing head is go-getter, typically high

indicators.note: beset by says the numeral is surrounded by the longing word

parts.note: to ache for something is to long for it
one is I as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter of the word over is dropped

explanation.surface: A go-getter tormented by longing, losing their head, often high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'typically high' points to the set phrase 'high achiever'.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-getter is an ambitious person who gets results, typically described as high-flying.

clue.text: Cold duck I sent back in Spanish snack food

indicators.note: in says the reversed letters go inside the snack

parts.note: a tapa is a small Spanish bar snack

indicators.note: sent back says these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Someone returns a cold duck dish served as Spanish tapas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns C, O, I into IOC, which goes inside TAPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapioca is a starchy food from cassava root, used in puddings.

clue.text: Surplus Sun deliveries

parts.note: over can mean surplus, left over
S is the abbreviation for Sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: Surplus Sunday newspaper deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, or deliveries, from one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Overs are sets of balls bowled in cricket, so they are made of deliveries.

clue.text: Yearn for change after smart deception

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind the word for smart

parts.note: chic means smart and stylish

indicators.note: for change says the letters of yearn are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Longing for change after a smart piece of deception.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicanery is trickery used to deceive, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Grant, we hear, is cut

indicators.note: we hear says the name is to be taken by its sound; that these words also read backwards to give the letters is a coincidence

parts.note: Hugh Grant is the English film actor

explanation.surface: A financial grant has been cut, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like money but is the actor's surname, pointing to his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To hew is to chop or cut with an axe, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Reduce high rent with a cut

indicators.note: high means intoxicated, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A demand to lower a high rent by making a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like it describes the rent but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To truncate something is to shorten it by cutting off part, to reduce it.

clue.text: Flamboyant jumper worn by company Charlie

indicators.note: worn by says the jumper wraps around the company letters, as a garment would

parts.note: a kangaroo, roo for short, is a jumper
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A showy jumper worn by someone called Charlie at the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like a sweater but is a kangaroo; 'worn by' has the animal wrapped around the company and Charlie letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is an ornate, highly decorated style, so it serves as flamboyant.

clue.text: Happy pop fans or what they're likely to be listening to

indicators.note: fans means spreads out, so the letters of pop are scattered into a new order

parts.words: what they're likely to be listening to
parts.note: pop fans are likely to be listening to a tune

explanation.surface: Happy pop fans, or the songs they'll be listening to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fans' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal on POP OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy in the old sense of lucky or well timed, so it matches timely.

clue.text: Bittersweet stuff, with old Left dividing people generally

indicators.note: dividing says the old and left letters split the word for people

parts.note: the masses are people in general

explanation.surface: A political taste: the old Left dividing the general populace.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the dark syrup from refining sugar, sweet with a bitter edge.

clue.text: Duty to get nails, as quoted

indicators.note: as quoted says the word is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: tacks are small nails

explanation.surface: A duty imposed on nails, as stated.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty is a levy charged by the state, such as on imports.

clue.text: Full tuna ban arranged involving Germany

indicators.note: involving says the rearranged letters wrap around the German letter
arranged says the letters of these words are put in a new order

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A complete tuna ban arranged with German involvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant means plentiful, existing in full measure.

clue.text: Psychology professor making a case for pain

indicators.note: making a case for says the two words enclose the answer, as a case holds its contents

explanation.surface: A psychology professor arguing the case for pain.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span the end of the first word and the start of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyp is British slang for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'.

clue.text: Part of the ear we note –- this may be a trap!

parts.note: the cob is the central part of an ear of corn
B is a note in the musical scale

explanation.surface: Something about part of the human ear, with a warning of a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ear' looks anatomical but means an ear of corn.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider's web is built to catch prey, so it is a trap.

clue.text: This might make you laugh: old school pudding is served up and there's no end to it

indicators.note: served up in a down clue says the letters are read upwards, in reverse
no end says the final letter of the pudding is removed

parts.note: sago pudding was a staple of old school dinners

explanation.surface: A comic memory of a school pudding served up endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's no end to it' cuts SAGO to SAG; 'is served up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughing gas, nitrous oxide, makes people giggle; gas also means great fun.

clue.text: It's biting as Spooner's sleeping?

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the word's parts are swapped, as Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: dormant means asleep or inactive
dormant means asleep or inactive

explanation.surface: A puzzling question whether something is biting while asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the D and M of DOR-MANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant wit is sharp and cutting, so biting in the sense of sarcastic.

clue.text: Scotch following chocolate: it could get you high

indicators.note: following puts the word for scotch after the chocolate

parts.note: Aero is a British bubbly chocolate bar
to scotch a plan is to foil it

explanation.surface: Whisky after chocolate could make you tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky but is the verb to thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerofoil is a wing shape that gives lift, so it gets an aircraft aloft.

clue.text: Accompany some corpse's cortege

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Following a funeral procession behind the coffin.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to go along with them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Bet on troops being amateurs

parts.note: to lay a bet is to place a wager
troops are soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Gambling on soldiers who are mere amateurs.
explanation.definitionFit: Laymen are non-professionals, people without expert training.

clue.text: The altogether bald head

parts.note: bald can mean bare or plain, so naked
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness place names

explanation.surface: Describing the whole of a bald head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The altogether' is the idiom 'in the altogether', meaning without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the altogether means stark nude, wearing nothing at all.

clue.text: A host (or half of them) give up –- no depth

indicators.note: half of takes the second two of the four letters
no says the depth letter is taken away

parts.note: to cede is to give up or surrender

explanation.surface: A host, or half of a group, having to yield without depth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of them' gives EM; CEDE without D gives CEE.
explanation.definitionFit: An emcee is a master of ceremonies, the presenter who hosts an event.

clue.text: Sycophant undergoes change of heart but provides hot drink

indicators.note: change of heart says the central letter is swapped for another

parts.note: a toady is a fawning sycophant

explanation.surface: A flatterer has a change of heart and offers a warming drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle A of TOADY becomes D.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddy is a hot drink of spirits, water, sugar and spice.

clue.text: A bash that's the opposite of friendly

parts.note: a bash is a party, a social gathering

explanation.surface: A party that turns out to be unfriendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' looks like a blow but is a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Asocial means avoiding company, the reverse of sociable.

clue.text: Drone can put out weapons

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are displaced into a new order

explanation.surface: A military drone can knock out weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance is military weapons and ammunition, especially artillery.

clue.text: Stress causes regret regularly

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter is taken, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Stress regularly leads to regret.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to insist on it firmly, to declare it.
